0. Input

Program:

int[] a = {4, 7, 2, 9};
int sum = 0, max = a[0];
for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
    sum += a[i];
    if (a[i] > max) max = a[i];
}
double avg = (double) sum / a.length;
System.out.println(sum + " " + max + " " + avg);

Question: Explain how each of sum, max and avg gets its value.

Student's answer: sum adds every element, giving 22. max starts at 4 and keeps the biggest, 9. For avg, sum / a.length is divided first as ints, 22 / 4 = 5, and then the (double) makes it 5.0 Settings: width 3, depth 3, prune llm, backend claude-cli, model claude-opus-5-5

right after for (...) or while (...). | right rule: A ; right after the loop header is a null (empty) loop body, so the statements written after it are not repeated by the loop. | | err:for_loop->WrongIterationCount | wrong rule: Updates the loop counter so that the loop runs the wrong number of times. | right rule: The init, test and update together decide the number of passes; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:for_loop->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:for_loop->ForIsConditional | wrong rule: The body of a for statement executes at most once. | right rule: The body of a for statement runs once for every pass on which the condition is true, which can be many times. | | mis:for_loop->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:for_loop->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:for_loop->ForWhileNotInterchangeable | wrong rule: Some loops can only be written with for, others only with while. | right rule: Any for loop can be rewritten as a while loop and vice versa; for just packages init, test and update. | | mis:for_loop->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:for_loop->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs;
